- There are no receipts or payment records. A bill only has a status: unpaid, paid or blocked.

## 1. Navigation
- **Layout:** in `App.tsx`, a native stack (L22, L104-128) wraps a material top-tab navigator placed at the bottom (L23, L68-81). Tabs can be swiped (`swipeEnabled: true, lazy: true`, L74), and the tab bar is the custom `BigTabBar` (L28-66).
- **Route params** (`src/navigation.ts`):
  - Tabs (L4-8): `Overview`, `Scan`, `Providers`. None take params.
  - Stack (L10-18):

    | Screen | Params |
    |---|---|
    | `Tabs` | optional nested tab target |
    | `Bill` | `{id, notice?}` |
    | `Dispute` | `{billId, anomalyId?}` |
    | `Offers` | `{billId}` |
    | `AutoPay` | `{billId, provider, suggestedMax}` |
    | `Provider` | `{slug, provider}` |
    | `AddProvider` | none |

  - `useStackNavigation()` (L23) gives stack navigation from tab screens, e.g. `navigate('Tabs', {screen:'Scan'})`.
- **Section 3** is the `Providers` tab (`ProvidersScreen`). Its label is "Furnizori", or "Istoric" in Senior mode (`mode.tsx` L195).
- **Top bar:** there is one shared native-stack header for every screen (`App.tsx` L105-112). It is styled from the theme and has `headerRight: ModeSwitcher`. Its title changes with the focused tab (L117-120), and Bill and Provider set their own title with `setOptions`. A search bar could go in that header (`headerRight`/`headerTitle`, or native-stack `headerSearchBarOptions`), or in a strip above the tab navigator inside `Tabs()`. Screens don't draw their own top bar.
- **Generations:** `src/mode.tsx`.
  - `Mode = 'genz' | 'millennial' | 'senior'` (L7). Each has its own colours and sizes in `THEMES` (L31-104); Senior has `fs` ×1.3 and `touch: 64`.
  - Each mode has its own wording in `COPY` (L109-229).
  - Screens call `useTheme()`, `useCopy()` and `useStyles(makeStyles)` (L269-276). The chosen mode is stored in AsyncStorage under `pago.mode`.
  - A search bar does **not** need 3 components. One component with theme tokens, plus new `COPY` strings (placeholder, mic label) per mode, is the existing pattern. Only `OverviewScreen` branches its layout on `t.mode` (L217/255/282).

## 2. Bill, provider history and month overview
- **`BillScreen`** (`src/screens/BillScreen.tsx`), params `{id, notice?}`.
  - Loads with `api.getBill(id)`, which calls `GET /api/bills/{id}/` (L53-62).
  - Also uses `api.ask`, `api.pay(id,'manual')`, `api.confirmBill`, `api.hasBillPdf`/`billPdfUrl` (L124-129) and `api.submitReading` (via `ReadingModal`).
  - In mock mode, only the latest bill per provider opens (`client.ts` L116-121).
- **`ProviderScreen`** (`src/screens/ProviderScreen.tsx`), params `{slug, provider}`.
  - Loads with `api.providerHistory(slug)`, which calls `GET /api/providers/{slug}/` (L29-39), plus `api.billStatuses()`.
  - Months are picked by tapping a `MonthBars` bar (L110-120), which shows a `SelectedBill` card (L126). The bill list is under "Toate facturile" (L143-150).
  - There is **no month param**. Pre-selecting a month would need a new `month?` param that sets the `selected` state (L27).
- **`OverviewScreen`** (`src/screens/OverviewScreen.tsx`) is a tab with **no params**.
  - Loads with `api.dashboard(month?)`, which calls `GET /api/dashboard/?month=YYYY-MM` (L39-44). It caches each month (L33) and changes month with `show(m)` (L56-69).
  - Opening it at a given month would mean adding `Overview: {month?: string}` to `TabParamList`.
- **`ProvidersScreen`**: `api.providers()` calls `GET /api/providers/`.
- **Backend `/bills/` filters:** `backend/bills/views.py` L44-56 supports only `?all=1` and `?source=upload|seed`. The default is the latest bill per provider. **There is no `provider=` or `month=` filter.** `/dashboard/` checks `month` against `YYYY-MM` and returns 400 `bad_month` otherwise (L177-179).
- **Endpoints** (`backend/bills/urls.py` L8-16): bills router, autopay-rules, `dashboard/`, `bills/&lt;id&gt;/pdf/`, `bills/&lt;id&gt;/files/&lt;index&gt;/`, `providers/`, `providers/&lt;slug&gt;/`. They are documented in `docs/API_V2.md` §2-§4.
- **Fallback when a v2 endpoint returns 404, and in mock mode** (`client.ts` L66-97, `src/api/derive.ts`):
  - It builds the data on the phone from `/bills/`, `/bills/?all=1` and each `/bills/{id}/`, cached for 30 s.
  - `derive.toPoints` (L55) produces flat points with `month: "YYYY-MM"`, `slug`, `status`, `audit_status`.
  - That makes it a ready-made searchable index of every bill by provider and month.

## 3. Payments and receipts
- There is nothing about a "chitanță" or receipt document. The backend mentions "receipt" only in the AI prompt (`backend/bills/services/ai.py` L135). `Icon` has a `'receipt'` glyph (`src/components/Icon.tsx` L4, L25).
- **Paid state:**
  - `BillStatus = 'unpaid'|'paid'|'blocked'` (`src/api/types.ts` L7). It appears on `BillSummary.status`, `DashboardSlice.status` (L199) and `ProviderBill.status` (L257).
  - `DashboardResponse.paid_total`/`unpaid_total` (L214-215).
  - Backend: `Bill.Status` (`backend/bills/models.py` L27-30, L58).
- **There are no `paid_at` or payment-history fields.** No receipt PDF either; `bills/{id}/pdf/` is the bill itself.
- **Where it shows in the UI:**
  - `BillScreen` L227-235: pay button, or `copy.paid`.
  - `ProviderScreen` `BillRow` L245: raw `bill.status` text.
  - `OverviewScreen` L117 and L287: Senior "Vă așteaptă N facturi de plată".
  - Pay calls: `api.pay` → `POST /bills/{id}/pay/ {mode}` returns `PayResponse {status, reasons}`; `AutoPayScreen` L27-34.

## 4. `src/api/client.ts`
- **Exports:** `API_URL` (L24), `MOCK` (L26), `ApiRequestError` (L40), `parseApiError` (L53), `api` (L112-246).
- **`api` methods:**

  | Method | Endpoint |
  |---|---|
  | `listBills` | `GET /bills/` |
  | `getBill(id)` | `GET /bills/{id}/` |
  | `scanBill(files)` | `POST /bills/scan/` (multipart, 120 s timeout) |
  | `dashboard(month?)` | `GET /dashboard/?month=` |
  | `providers()` | `GET /providers/` |
  | `providerHistory(slug)` | `GET /providers/{slug}/` |
  | `ask(billId, {question?, line_item_id?})` | `POST /bills/{id}/ask/` |
  | `dispute` | `POST /bills/{id}/dispute/` |
  | `offers` | `GET /bills/{id}/offers/` |
  | `confirmBill` | `POST /bills/{id}/confirm/` |
  | `billStatuses()` | `GET /bills/?all=1` (30 s cache) |
  | `billPdfUrl` / `hasBillPdf` | `/bills/{id}/pdf/` (HEAD for the check) |
  | `submitReading` | `POST /bills/{id}/reading/` |
  | `pay(id, mode)` | `POST /bills/{id}/pay/` |
  | `createAutoPayRule` | `POST /autopay-rules/` |

- **Mock mode:** turned on by `EXPO_PUBLIC_MOCK === '1'`.
  - Imports `../../../shared/fixtures/bills.json` and `bill_details.json` (L2-3).
  - `delay()` fakes latency (L29). Each method has an inline `MOCK ? delay(...) : request(...)` branch, and the v2 endpoints go through `derive`.
  - `.env.example` lists `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL`, `EXPO_PUBLIC_MOCK` and `EXPO_PUBLIC_USE_RN_FETCH`.
  - `OverviewScreen` L215 shows a "MOD DEMO" banner in mock mode.
- **Errors:** `request()` (L31-38) throws `parseApiError(status, text)`. That reads v2 `{code, detail, existing_bill_id}` or v1 `{detail}`, and falls back to the raw text (first 200 chars) or `HTTP &lt;status&gt;`. Screens usually just show `String(e?.message ?? e)`.

## 5. Packages and config
- **Expo SDK 58** (`expo ~58.0.25`), RN 0.88.1, React 19.3.
- **expo-\* modules:** only `expo-document-picker`, `expo-image-picker` and `expo-status-bar`. The lockfile adds nothing else besides `expo-image-loader` and the core modules.
- **No microphone or speech package:** no `expo-av`, `expo-audio`, `expo-speech`, `expo-speech-recognition` or `@react-native-voice`. A grep for speech/audio/voice/microphone finds nothing.
- **`app.json`** has no `plugins` and no permissions (no microphone, no camera entries).
- **Constraint:** `AGENTS.md` says the app "Must keep working in Expo Go (no custom native modules)" and to use `npx expo install`.
  - `expo-speech-recognition` is a third-party native module, so it won't run in Expo Go.
  - What fits Expo Go: record with `expo-audio` (bundled in Expo Go, I believe; check the SDK 58 docs) and send the audio to a new backend endpoint for transcription, e.g. with Gemini.
  - Speech-to-text from the phone keyboard's dictation into a plain `TextInput` also works with no package.

## 6. Reusable building blocks
- **Bill rows:**
  - `ProviderScreen` `BillRow` (L208-249, not exported) shows month, chips, total, delta and status. `rowTone()` is exported (L202).
  - `OverviewScreen` breakdown rows (L168-178) show a colour dot, provider, `ReviewMark`, `SeverityBadge` and total.
  - `ProvidersScreen` provider rows (L107-135).
- **Provider visuals:** `ProviderAvatar({provider, category, size})` draws initials on the category colour (`src/components/ProviderAvatar.tsx`). There are no logos.
- **Provider matching** (`src/providersRo.ts`):
  - `RO_PROVIDERS` with aliases (L15-32).
  - `fold()` ignores case and diacritics (L35).
  - **`searchProviders(query, category?)`** scores names and aliases (L43-54). It can be reused directly to turn spoken or typed text into a provider.
  - `slugify` is in `src/api/derive.ts` L36.
- **Months and money** (`src/theme.ts`):
  - `monthLabel("2026-10")` gives "octombrie 2026", or "oct" when short (L19).
  - `monthName` (L23).
  - The `LONG`/`SHORT` Romanian month arrays (L15-16) are not exported, but are useful for parsing "factura din octombrie".
  - `money`, `deltaLabel`, `deltaColor`, `category` labels and colours, `tabular`.
- **Other components** in `src/components/`:
  - `Toast` (`{message, duration}`; remount with `key` to replay; L6).
  - `Button` (variants primary, secondary, ghost).
  - `ConfirmDialog`, `SeverityBadge`, `ReviewMark` (in `ValidationCard`).
  - `Icon` (no mic or search glyph yet).
  - `MonthPager`, `charts/MonthBars`.
  - `ModeSwitcher`: its Modal bottom-sheet pattern could serve a search overlay.
- **Theme tokens:** `bg, surface, surface2, text, muted, border, accent, onAccent, highlight, sev[...], radius, inner, pad, fs(), touch` (`mode.tsx` L9-27). `isFlagged` is in `src/validation.ts`.

## 7. Existing "ask AI" UI
- **Ask bar:** `BillScreen` L238-259, pinned at the bottom.
  - A horizontal row of suggested-question chips from `questionsFor(bill, t.mode)` (`src/questions.ts` L26; 2 in Senior mode, 4 otherwise, built from category and anomalies).
  - A `TextInput` with `copy.askPlaceholder` and an "Întreabă" button.
- **Answer card:** L195-225 shows the question, answer, source chips and `suggested_actions` buttons, which go to `onAction` (L95-109) to navigate to Dispute, Offers or AutoPay, or to open the reading modal.
- **API:** `api.ask(billId, {question?, line_item_id?})` → `POST /bills/{id}/ask/` returns `AskResponse {question, line_item, answer, sources[], suggested_actions[]}` (`types.ts` L133-139). Tapping a bill line asks about that line (L191).
- It only works per bill; there is no global, bill-independent AI query endpoint.

[2026-11-17 08:35:44] CLAUDE:
The demo can show anomalies of two different kinds, and a bill edited with AI can trigger either one, depending on how it's edited.

## What we have now

**1. Bill audit (`backend/bills/services/audit.py`).** These are plain rules in code, with no AI: they compare the bill with your history and with the market. This is the colored badge on the bill:

| Check | When it fires | Level |
|---|---|---|
| `estimated_index` | the index is estimated, and consumption is >30% above your real average | 🔴 critical (otherwise 🟡) |
| `price_spike` | the total is >20% above last month, and the growth is not explained by consumption | 🟡 |
| `above_market` | the price per kWh with all taxes is >10% above market (1.33 lei/kWh for electricity) | 🟡 + cheaper offers |
| `extra_service` | a paid add-on that appeared on the bill recently | 🟡 + "cancel" |
| `penalty` | there are late-payment penalties | 🟡 |
| `above_county_average` | consumption >30% above the county average | info |

**2. Discrepancies in the provider history (Furnizori tab):** a sudden jump in the total (≥50% is 🔴), the price per unit changed, a jump in consumption, the index doesn't continue from the last bill, a new line on the bill, a missing month.

What fires on the October demo bills right now:
- **PPC 🔴:** estimated index of 350 kWh against an average of 177; plus above market.
- **Engie 🟡:** +42.2% while consumption grew only 8%, the price per kWh changed; plus above market and 86.67 lei of savings.
- **Digi 🟡:** "Extra TV + Antivirus" at 15 lei/month for 6 months.
- **Apa Brașov 🟢:** all normal.

## What your edit with a very high price will trigger

It depends on how you edit:
- **Edited consistently** (price per m³ → line amount → VAT → total): this is a real overcharge. The **audit** catches it: `price_spike`, plus "the total jumped" and "the unit price went up" in the history.
- **Only the total changed** (the lines no longer add up): this is a forged or broken bill. **Validation** catches it: "the lines don't add up to the total", status "De verificat". That's a strong point for the pitch: the AI reads, the rules check the bill's own math.

Image AI often redraws neighbouring digits too (customer code, dates), so the result is unpredictable. Better to rehearse it before going on stage.

## What I propose for the demo

Take **Apa Brașov**, which is green now, and turn it red live:
1. Show Apa as 🟢 normal.
2. Scan an "expensive" October water bill with the water price changed from 5.71 to about 14.90 lei/m³. The total goes from 72 lei to about 136 lei (+86%) with the same consumption. Expected: 🟡 "the bill went up 86%, but consumption didn't", and 🔴 "the total jumped" in the history.
3. Optionally, a second file where only the total was changed by hand. The app shows "De verificat: the lines don't add up to the total".

I'd make both files myself with our PDF generator, so the numbers are exact and predictable, then run them through the real scan and pre-warm the cache so the scan on stage is instant.

**Two catches to keep in mind:**
- **Duplicates:** a second, different edit of the same Apa October bill gets 409 "Ai scanat deja factura asta" against the first upload. Between rehearsals, reset with `seed_demo`.
- **PPC:** in the demo you scan the real PPC photos, so don't make the edited bill from PPC October. It will also get a 409.

         seen, out = set(), []
         for m in [settings.GEMINI_MODEL, *settings.GEMINI_FALLBACK_MODELS]:

                 out.append(m)

         """Try the main model, then each fallback, when Gemini says 'busy' (5xx) or 'too many requests' (429).
         Other errors (bad key, bad request) are raised at once: another model wouldn't fix them."""

                     last = e
                     continue
                 raise
         raise AIUnavailable(str(last))

     async function appendFile(form: FormData, field: string, file: UploadFile) {
       if (Platform.OS === 'web') {
         // On web the picker gives a blob:/data: URI; FormData needs the actual Blob.
         const blob = await (await fetch(file.uri)).blob();
         form.append(field, blob, file.name);
       } else {
         // React Native's FormData accepts {uri, name, type} objects for files.
         form.append(field, { uri: file.uri, name: file.name, type: file.mimeType } as unknown as Blob);
       }
     }

[2026-11-17 09:16:00] CLAUDE:
I fixed both problems on the backend. The colleague's frontend was already pulled: main includes their commit.

**Why voice "loaded forever" and the scan said "aglomerat"**

Gemini is overloaded right now. I checked live:
- the main model answers;
- the second (`gemini-3.6-flash`) returns 503 "high demand";
- the third (`gemini-4-hydrogen`) took **107 seconds** to answer "Say OK".

Our backend had no timeout on Gemini calls. When the main model got busy, the request fell through to the slow model and hung for minutes. That's the endless voice spinner. When all models failed, the scan of the screenshot got 503 "Serviciul AI e foarte aglomerat" instead of "Nu pare o factură".

**What I changed (commit 45cabd5):**
- **Time limits:** each Gemini call now has a time limit per model and in total:
  - voice: at most 12 s per model, 25 s in total;
  - scan: 40 s per model, 60 s in total;
  - questions: 15 s per model, 30 s in total.

  When the time runs out, the server answers with a clear error at once instead of hanging.
- **A second try on the main model:** a 503 from it is usually a short spike, so it gets tried once more before falling back to the slower models.
- **Live check:** voice answered in 2.5 s, and a screenshot that isn't a bill gives 422 "Nu pare o factură de utilități sau telecom" in 13 s.

**The app's own bug, for the colleague (I'm not touching the frontend):**
- In `mobile/src/screens/SearchScreen.tsx`, the voice `send` function only clears the spinner if no other search started meanwhile: `finally { if (seq.current === id) setThinking(false) }`.
- If a text search starts while voice is waiting for the answer, the spinner never goes away.
- The fix: in that `finally`, call `setThinking(false)` with no condition.

**Two important things:**
1. **The phone talks to the colleague's laptop** (`172.20.10.2:8000`). On your laptop the server isn't running: it crashed back yesterday in the "backend" tab. So for the fix to work, the colleague needs to get it and restart the server. After you push:

  -> ## 3. `GET /api/providers/` – provider list
     
     One entry per provider, **sorted by `last_period_end` desc, then provider name**.
     
     ```json
     [
       {
         "provider": "PPC",
         "slug": "ppc",
         "category": "electricity",
         "bills_count": 12,
         "last_bill_id": 24,
         "last_period_end": "2026-10-31",
         "last_total": "501.85",
         "average_total": "268.40",
         "trend_pct": 87.0,
         "audit_status": "critical",
         "anomalies_count": 3,
         "totals": ["246.62", "279.61", "...", "501.85"]
       }
     ]
     ```
     
     | Field | Rule |
     |---|---|
     | `average_total` | average of the provider's bill totals **excluding the latest** |
     | `trend_pct` | `(last_total − average_total) / average_total × 100` |
     | `audit_status`, `anomalies_count` | from the **latest** bill's audit (`anomalies_count` counts `warning` + `critical`, not `info`) |
     | `totals` | last 12 bill totals, **oldest first** – the sparkline on the card |

The provider archive is done on the backend: commit b65308d, 82 tests pass. The contract for the colleague is in `docs/API_V2.md` §8.

**How it works:**

| Call | Does |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/providers/{slug}/archive/` | puts the provider in the archive, returns its card with `archived: true` |
| `DELETE /api/providers/{slug}/archive/` | takes it out of the archive, returns the card with `archived: false` |

- In `GET /api/providers/`, each card has new fields `archived` and `archived_at`. Archived providers go **to the bottom of the list**; the order among them stays the same.
- `GET /api/providers/{slug}/` also returns `archived`, so the provider screen can show a "Scoate din arhivă" button.
- **Only the look changes:** bills, PDFs, history, the dashboard totals and search stay as they are. The tests check that.
- A provider with no bills gives 404 `unknown_provider`. A repeated archive or unarchive call isn't an error.
- `seed_demo` empties the archive, like the rest of the demo data.
- **Texts for the app**, as suggestions: "Mută în arhivă" / "Scoate din arhivă", and the "Arhivă" section at the bottom of the list.

[2026-11-17 09:44:21] CLAUDE:
The colleague's slowness has two possible causes. I fixed the one on the backend; the other needs one check on their laptop.

**1. A bug in my previous fix (fixed, commit 58a7619).** Right now `3.5-flash-lite` either answers 503 or takes about 10 s, while `3.1-flash-lite` answers in about 1 s. Before, a slow main model got a second try and used up the whole time budget before reaching the fast model, so the app got "aglomerat". Now:
- the main model is retried only after a quick 503;
- after a timeout or a 429, it goes straight to the next model;
- the per-model limit is 10 s for voice and 12 s for questions.

Live through the real endpoints, even while `3.5-flash-lite` answered 503: **voice 1.4–2.5 s, a question 4.5–8 s**.

**2. The colleague's key may have run out of its free limit.** Gemini then answers 429, and we also show that as "aglomerat". To check, I added a diagnostic: `ai_check --models` prints the model list their `.env` actually uses and, for each model, either OK with the time or the error with an explanation.

[2026-11-17 10:26:19] CLAUDE:
I checked all three cases live with Gemini on a throwaway copy of the demo data. Two work fine, and one has a hole: the extra bills silently disappear.

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| **A.** Several bills in one request (Engie PDF + Digi PDF) | ⚠️ Saved as **one Engie bill**. Digi silently disappears, and the Digi page stays attached to the Engie bill as a "second page" |
| **B.** One bill + 9 pages of text (10 pages, ~44,000 characters) | ✅ Read exactly: Engie, 352.53 lei, all 9 lines, in 16 s |
| **C.** The same with 11 pages | ✅ Refused at once: 400 "Factura are 11 pagini; trimite cel mult 10." |
| **D.** One PDF with 3 bills inside (Engie + Digi + Apa) | ⚠️ Saved **only Engie** (the first). Digi and Apa disappear, with no warning |

**Why:** the scan is built on the rule "one request = one bill, and several files are pages of that bill". Gemini sees several bills, picks one, and the user thinks everything was scanned.

**Other limits that already hold:**
- at most 10 files per request;
- at most 10 pages in total;
- 10 MB per file and 25 MB in total;
- at most 60 lines per bill;
- the whole scan has at most 60 s.

**What I propose (~20 min of backend, no app changes):**
- Gemini additionally reports whether the document holds other, distinct bills: a different provider, customer code or period.
- If it does, the scan refuses with **422 `several_bills`** and saves nothing, for example: "Am găsit 3 facturi într-un singur fișier (Engie, Digi, Apa Brasov). Trimite fiecare factură separat."
- The app already shows backend errors as text, so the colleague doesn't need to change anything.
- Splitting a file into several bills automatically would be heavier (several Gemini calls and a different response format for the app), so I'd leave that until after the hackathon.
